site: AP-9, Arcadia Planitia (SpaceX Starship candidate landing site)
height_decode: v = R*256 + G (B = 0); metres = lo + v/65535*(hi-lo); metres are relative to the MOLA areoid
projection: orthographic (tangent plane) centred on (lat, lon) on the 3396.19 km Mars 2000 sphere; image row 0 = north edge, +x = east, +y = north; pixel centres at ((i+0.5)/n - 0.5)*extent. Heights are NOT curvature-corrected: the sphere falls away from the tangent plane by r^2/(2R) (~66 m at 20 km, ~13.2 km at the 300 km context edge).

notes: height.png: HRSC/MOLA blended DEM 200 m, bilinear to 56.6 m/px. color.webp: Murray Lab global CTX mosaic V01 (5 m/px, quads E-160_N40, E-160_N36), 5x5 box-averaged then bilinear to 28.3 m/px, greyscale, 0.5-99.5 percentile stretch. tint.webp and context-color.webp: Viking MDIM 2.1 colour mosaic (~232 m native, Trek zoom 7 ~325 m/px); use tint as a low-frequency colour multiplier for the greyscale CTX. context-height.png: HRSC/MOLA blend, 1 km box-averaged, bilinear to 1172 m/px. CTX nodata (0.01% of color.webp) filled with Viking luminance. No HiRISE/CTX DTM is openly published for AP-9, so height is the 200 m HRSC/MOLA blend only. Over these very smooth plains (~300 m total relief) the HRSC strips show as rectangular patches of ~10-20 m stereo noise against smoother MOLA-only areas; low-relief features seen in CTX (e.g. the ~7 km bright-rimmed ghost crater near the north edge) have little or no DEM expression. Let CTX carry the fine detail (e.g. derive a normal map from color.webp). color.webp crosses the CTX quad seam at 40.0 N (row ~1064 of 2048); it is tone-continuous. Extent is 58 km (not 60) so the patch stays inside CTX quad E-160 (lon < -156 E).
